newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George, Advance merger terms set.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George, Advance merger terms set.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Ltd said on Monday that Advance Bank ordinary shareholders would receive 0.625 of a new St George Bank ordinary share, A$2.10 in cash from St George and a 20 cent per share special dividend for each Advance Bank share as payment for the planned merger of the two banks.
The special dividend would be franked to about 60 percent.
Advance Bank ordinary shareholders would also receive an interim fully franked dividend of 20 cents per share.
The terms set were based on the weighted average St George Bank share price, ex-final dividend, in the 20 business days up to January 3, of A$7.90.

"As a result of this being below A$8.00, Advance shareholders will receive 228.2 million new St George Ordinary Shares, being the maximum number of shares to be issued as consideration," St George said.
The interim dividend for Advance shareholders was expected to be paid on January 28 and the final merger payment was expected in February, they said.
St George also said it had received final approvals from the Treasurer and the Governor General for the merger.
Advance Bank shareholders gave their initial approval in late December for the A$2.65 billion merger to create Australia's fifth largest bank.

The New South Wales Supreme Court is expected to consider the merger's scheme of arrangement later on Monday and two more meetings of Advance Bank holders are due to be held on January 13 to finally approve the merger.
National Australia Bank Ltd, which holds 6.8 percent of St George, has also said it owns three percent of Advance.
NAB, which is seen as interested in buying regional banks, has not said whether it opposes the merger.
